answer: An agent market can require every bidding identity to lock a fixed token bond for 30 days, with each bond assigned to one public key and unusable by other accounts until release. A cipher can hide an agent’s messages, but it cannot supply the required collateral. An attacker may forge a gale of identities, yet activating 1,000 of them requires 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and imposing financing costs throughout the lock period.
